title: Reading Test 8: Sleep and Effective Learning
passage: Sleep has a strong influence on learning, but its role is sometimes underestimated by students. When people study new material, the brain does not simply store information at the moment of reading or listening. Important changes continue to happen after study sessions have ended.

Researchers often describe sleep as a period of memory consolidation. During this process, the brain strengthens some new connections and weakens others. This may help learners remember important information while forgetting details that are less useful.

Sleep can also affect attention. A student who sleeps poorly may read the same paragraph several times without understanding it fully. In contrast, a rested student is more likely to notice relationships between ideas and correct errors during practice.

Many students try to compensate for limited time by studying late into the night. This may increase the number of hours spent with books, but it can reduce the quality of learning the following day. Short review sessions over several days are often more effective than one long session before a test.

Good study routines therefore include both active practice and recovery. Testing oneself, explaining ideas aloud, and reviewing mistakes are useful strategies, but they work best when combined with enough sleep. Learning is not only about effort; it is also about allowing the brain time to organise what has been learned.

questionGroups.title: Questions 1-4
questionGroups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Choose TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

questions.question: The brain continues to process information after study sessions end.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 says important changes continue after study sessions have ended.

questions.question: Memory consolidation involves strengthening some connections and weakening others.
Studying late at night always improves learning quality the next day.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 says it can reduce the quality of learning the following day.

questions.question: The passage says every student needs exactly eight hours of sleep.
questions.explanation: The passage discusses enough sleep but gives no exact number.
